title: Display total trip expenses summary
body:
As a user, I want to see the total expenses for the trip so that I can understand overall spending.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Total expense amount is displayed at the top of the Expense tab
- Value updates when expenses are added, edited, or deleted
- Handles empty state (shows $0 or placeholder)
- Value reflects sum of all expenses tied to the tripId

title: Implement query to calculate total expenses by tripId
body: Write a database query (Room DAO or SQL) that aggregates the sum of all expense totals filtered by tripId. Ensure null-safe aggregation and efficient performance for larger datasets.

title: Expose aggregated total in ViewModel
body: Add a function or LiveData/StateFlow in the ViewModel that retrieves and exposes the total expense value from the repository layer. Ensure it updates reactively when underlying data changes.

title: Build UI component to display total expenses
body: Create a composable or UI component that renders the total expense value prominently. Include formatting (currency), styling, and support for loading/empty states.

title: Display per-person spending vs budget
body:
As a user, I want to see how much each person has spent compared to their budget so that I can track contributions.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Each person shows total spent and budget amount
- Data is accurate and reflects all expenses
- Updates dynamically when expenses change
- Handles cases where budget is missing (shows default or placeholder)

title: Aggregate expenses per person
body: Write logic (SQL or repository layer) to group expenses by personId and calculate total amount spent per person. Ensure compatibility with split logic if needed.

title: Join expense data with budget data
body: Combine aggregated expense totals with budget data per person (via JOIN or ViewModel mapping). Ensure correct matching on personId and null-safe handling.

title: Map aggregated data into UI model
body: Transform combined expense and budget data into a UI-friendly model (e.g., data class) that includes person name, spent amount, and budget.

title: Display budget progress bars per person
body:
As a user, I want to see a visual progress bar for each person’s budget usage so that I can quickly assess spending.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Progress bar reflects percentage of spent vs budget
- Updates dynamically with data changes
- Handles divide-by-zero or missing budget cases gracefully
- UI is visually consistent across users

title: Compute budget usage percentage per person
body: Implement logic to calculate percentage = spent / budget for each person. Ensure proper handling of zero or null budget values.
parent: Display budget progress bars per person

title: Build reusable progress bar UI component
body: Create a reusable UI component (Compose or XML) for displaying progress bars with labels and percentages.
parent: Display budget progress bars per person

title: Bind progress data to UI components
body: Connect ViewModel data to progress bar UI, ensuring recomposition/reactivity when values change.
parent: Display budget progress bars per person

title: Display list of all total expenses
body:
As a user, I want to see a list of all expenses so that I can review trip spending.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Expenses are displayed in a scrollable list
- Each item shows name, total, and payer
- List updates when data changes
- Empty state is handled gracefully

title: Fetch all expenses by tripId
body: Implement DAO/repository method to retrieve all expenses associated with a tripId, ordered by createdAt by default.
parent: Display list of all total expenses

title: Build expense preview card UI
body: Create a UI card component displaying expense name, total amount, and payer. Ensure proper layout and styling.
parent: Display list of all total expenses

title: Bind expense data to list UI
body: Connect fetched expense data to a LazyColumn/RecyclerView, ensuring efficient rendering and updates.
parent: Display list of all total expenses

title: View detailed information for a selected expense
body:
As a user, I want to view detailed information about an expense so that I can understand all associated data.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Clicking an expense opens a detail modal or screen
- Displays name, total, payer, logistics item (optional), split, and notes
- UI is consistent and scrollable if needed

title: Create expense detail modal or screen
body: Design and implement a modal or navigation destination for displaying detailed expense information.
parent: View detailed information for a selected expense

title: Implement navigation to detail view
body: Add click handlers and navigation logic to open the detail view when a user selects an expense.
parent: View detailed information for a selected expense

title: Populate detail view with full expense data
body: Fetch and bind all relevant fields (including optional logistics and split data) into the detail UI.
parent: View detailed information for a selected expense

title: Display split expenses per person
body:
As a user, I want to see how each expense is split per person so that I know individual shares.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Each expense shows per-person share
- Data reflects correct split calculations
- Updates dynamically when data changes

title: Compute per-person share for each expense
body: Implement logic to calculate each person's share of an expense based on split rules (equal/custom).

title: Transform split data into UI-friendly format
body: Map split calculation results into a structure suitable for display in the UI (e.g., per-person rows).

title: View detailed split breakdown for an expense
body:
As a user, I want to see detailed split information so that I understand how costs are divided.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Detail view includes split breakdown per person
- Matches total expense amount
- Reuses consistent UI patterns

title: Reuse expense detail UI for split view
body: Adapt existing detail UI to support split-focused display without duplication of code.
parent: View detailed split breakdown for an expense

title: Ensure split breakdown is displayed in detail view
body: Extend data binding to include per-person split values and display them clearly.
parent: View detailed split breakdown for an expense

title: Create a new expense with full details
body:
As a user, I want to add a new expense so that I can track spending.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Plus button is visible and accessible
- Form captures all required fields
- Validation prevents invalid input
- New expense appears in list after creation

title: Add floating action button for expense creation
body: Add a FAB (+) to the Expense screen that triggers navigation to the create expense form.
parent: Create a new expense with full details

title: Build expense creation form UI
body: Design and implement form fields for name, total, payer, split, optional logistics item, and notes.
parent: Create a new expense with full details

title: Implement input validation for expense form
body: Add validation rules (non-empty fields, valid amounts, valid splits) and show error messages to users.
parent: Create a new expense with full details

title: Insert new expense and split records into database
body: Persist expense and associated split data using DAO methods, ensuring referential integrity.
parent: Create a new expense with full details

title: Refresh UI after expense creation
body: Trigger ViewModel/state updates so the new expense appears immediately in the list.
parent: Create a new expense with full details

title: Edit an existing expense
body:
As a user, I want to edit an expense so that I can correct mistakes.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Edit icon is visible on expense cards
- Form is pre-filled with existing data
- Changes persist after saving
- List updates automatically

title: Add edit icon to expense preview card
body: Update UI to include an edit (pencil) icon on each expense card in total expense view.

title: Pre-fill edit form with existing expense data
body: Load selected expense data into the form fields for editing.

title: Update expense and split records in database
body: Implement DAO update methods for expense and associated splits, ensuring consistency.

title: Refresh UI after editing expense
body: Ensure UI reflects updated data immediately after saving changes.

title: Delete an existing expense
body:
As a user, I want to delete an expense so that I can remove incorrect entries.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Delete icon is visible
- Confirmation dialog is shown before deletion
- Expense is removed from list
- Associated split records are also deleted

title: Add delete icon to expense preview card
body: Add a delete (trash) icon to each expense card in the total expenses view.

title: Implement confirmation dialog before deletion
body: Show a modal dialog prompting user confirmation before deleting an expense.

title: Delete expense and related split records from database
body: Implement DAO logic to delete expense and cascade delete associated splits.

title: Refresh UI after deleting expense
body: Ensure the UI updates immediately after deletion to remove the expense from the list.

title: Filter total expenses by payer
body:
As a user, I want to filter expenses by payer so that I can focus on specific contributions.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Filter control is available
- Selecting a payer updates the list
- Clearing filter restores full list

title: Build payer filter UI control
body: Create dropdown/chips allowing user to select payer filter.

title: Store and manage selected filter state
body: Maintain filter selection in ViewModel and persist across recompositions.

title: Apply filtering logic to expense list
body: Filter displayed expenses based on selected payer using ViewModel or query-level filtering.

title: Filter split expenses by person
body:
As a user, I want to filter split expenses by person so that I can view individual shares.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Filter applies to split expense view
- List updates correctly based on selection

title: Extend filtering logic to split data
body: Apply selected person filter to computed split dataset before rendering UI.

title: Sort expenses by creation date
body:
As a user, I want to sort expenses chronologically so that I can view them in order.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Supports ascending and descending order
- Sorting persists during session
- Applies to both total and split views

title: Add sort control to UI
body: Create toggle or dropdown to switch between ascending/descending sort.

title: Apply sorting logic to expense data
body: Sort expense list in ViewModel or via DAO query using createdAt field.

title: Group total expenses by payer
body:
As a user, I want to group expenses by payer so that I can understand spending distribution.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Expenses are grouped under payer headers
- Groups update dynamically
- Works with filtering and sorting

title: Transform expense list into grouped structure
body: Convert flat expense list into grouped map keyed by payer.

title: Add grouped section headers to UI
body: Render section headers and grouped items in list UI.

title: Group split expenses by person
body:
As a user, I want to group split expenses by person so that I can see individual cost breakdowns.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Split expenses grouped by person
- Accurate aggregation per group
- UI clearly separates groups

title: Transform split data into grouped structure
body: Group computed split data by personId into UI-friendly sections.

title: Update UI to render grouped split sections
body: Modify split expense UI to display grouped sections with headers.
